items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: I know that story about Nelson for fact because people talk about it quite often.

ctx.x: Yeah, to sit and be in the middle of that and realize the skill it took to know what not to write as well as what to write.

Yeah. Hundred percent. And you know I mean the one — Nelson Riddle comes to mind — I mean such a great arranger. And you know he was a trombone player, not a particularly great trombone player, but he was a trombone player, typically playing in a big band section, probably playing third trombone. And the way he learned how to write was he would write on little pieces of — you know like a single stave — and just write out some voicings. And he would get done with a rehearsal and just ask the guys to stick around…
You were horn-mates with Tim Ries is that correct?
